questions.title: Function lost when all vagal output to the gut is eliminated
questions.question: A stroke completely eliminates all vagal output to the gastrointestinal tract. Which function is most likely to be totally eliminated?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Gastrin release can still be driven by luminal peptides acting directly on antral G cells and by local reflexes, so it is not totally eliminated.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Pancreatic bicarbonate secretion is driven largely by secretin released in response to duodenal acid, a hormonal pathway independent of the vagus.
explanations.C: Correct. The vagus directly innervates the striated muscle of the pharynx and upper oesophagus and coordinates swallowing and primary oesophageal peristalsis. Losing all vagal output abolishes this centrally programmed primary peristalsis. It is therefore the function most completely eliminated.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Secondary oesophageal peristalsis is a local stretch reflex triggered by a retained bolus and can occur through the enteric nervous system without vagal input, so it persists.

questions.learning_objective: State that the vagus coordinates primary oesophageal peristalsis, whereas secondary peristalsis is a local reflex that survives vagotomy.

questions.title: Agent that virtually eliminates gastric-phase acid secretion
questions.question: The gastric phase accounts for about 60 percent of the acid response to a meal. Which substance can virtually eliminate acid secretion during the gastric phase?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Blocking gastrin removes only one stimulatory pathway; histamine- and acetylcholine-driven acid secretion continues.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Atropine blocks the muscarinic (vagal) pathway but not the histamine and gastrin pathways, so acid secretion is reduced, not eliminated.
explanations.C: Incorrect. An H2 blocker removes the histamine pathway but leaves acetylcholine- and gastrin-driven secretion, so acid output is only lowered.
explanations.D: Correct. A proton pump inhibitor blocks the parietal-cell H+/K+ ATPase, the final common step of acid secretion. Because every stimulatory pathway ultimately works through this pump, inhibiting it can virtually eliminate acid secretion. The other agents block only one upstream pathway each and cannot abolish secretion.

questions.learning_objective: Explain that a proton pump inhibitor blocks the final common H+/K+ ATPase step, so it can virtually eliminate gastric acid secretion where single-pathway blockers cannot.

questions.title: Agent that both damages the mucosal barrier and stimulates acid
questions.question: Which substance can both damage the gastric mucosal barrier and stimulate gastric acid secretion?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Bile salts do damage the mucosal barrier, but they have no clinically significant effect to stimulate gastric acid secretion.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Epidermal growth factor strengthens and repairs the mucosal barrier rather than damaging it.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Gastrin stimulates acid secretion, but it strengthens (through its trophic effect) rather than damages the mucosal barrier.
explanations.D: Correct. Helicobacter pylori produces urease, generating ammonia that is converted to ammonium in the acid environment and damages the surface epithelial cells and the mucosal barrier. It also increases gastric acid secretion, probably by increasing parietal-cell mass. It is therefore the single agent that both damages the barrier and stimulates acid.
